native_reference.relevant_anchor: The retained scalar sender records that the ArrayDim!=1 branch writes one additional archive byte; its primary reference is selector plus 11-bit actor-channel or 31-bit package index, with no caller RPC-presence bit.
native_reference.scope_limit: The cited retained contract primarily documents scalar ObjectProperty framing. It does not by itself establish runtime use of this new array encoder.

reviewed_changes.observation: New ArrayObjectProperty carries field_id, array_dim, element_index, and the existing tagged primary reference. API comment explicitly specifies bounded field id, raw 8-bit index, no alignment/terminator/RPC presence, positive limits, index<dimension and <=255, and caller-owned schema/ID/reference validation.
New function is still a not_implemented scaffold. The expected RED tests cannot pass until parent integrates an implementation; this review is not acceptance.
The ten new cases use fixed expected byte vectors rather than using BitWriter to generate the expected payloads.

oracle_checks.result: Consistent. For bound 35, value 31 takes five bits under the existing value-dependent BitWriter::write_bounded algorithm; value 0 takes six. The field-zero/bound-one case correctly omits only the field-ID bits.

Consistent with the specified RAW8 framing: tests place the full index byte after the bounded ID at the current bit position, do not align it, accept index 255 when dimension is 512, and reject index 256 rather than truncating it.

Consistent with existing object reference writer: actor references use a selector plus bounded 11-bit channel (12 bits total); package references use selector plus bounded 31-bit index (32 bits total). The fixed literals and the documented expected totals (25 bits actor, 45 bits package for field31/bound35 plus index byte) agree with LSB-first placement.

Tests cover ordered duplicate records with no alignment, an opaque suffix appended at the 25-bit boundary, exact and one-bit-short aggregate budgets, positive limits even for empty spans, and zero high tail bits in literal vectors. The suffix test uses the existing writer/reader only to append/read the suffix; it separately checks the record against a fixed literal.

Tests cover ID equal to/exceeding the exclusive bound, non-array dimensions, index equal to dimension, index not representable by one byte, invalid actor/package ranges, and invalid later records without a returned partial payload.

limitations: No literal/oracle contradiction was found in the ten new cases during this source review.
The array byte semantics are being checked against the supplied retained framing evidence and the existing wire primitives; no new native extraction or runtime observation was performed.
The active implementation is only the not_implemented scaffold, and no tests were executed; the new feature remains unverified.
This review says nothing about effective field IDs, eligibility, expected class resolution, actor creation, possession, or gameplay behavior; the API comment leaves those to the caller.
